item.title: Medicare: HHS and CMS Should Better Manage Fraud Risks
item.description:
What GAO Found
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)—within the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)—and its various contractors oversee the traditional Medicare Fee-for-Service program (Medicare). CMS reported spending nearly $481 billion on benefits for about 34 million Medicare beneficiaries in 2025.
CMS uses the Vulnerability Management (VM) Process within the Center for Program Integrity (CPI) to manage fraud risks. However, this process is broader in scope and does not fully reflect the range of fraud risks facing Medicare. Without fully identifying and assessing fraud risks consistent with leading fraud risk management practices, CPI is missing opportunities to fully mitigate fraud risks before they materialize into significant fraud in Medicare. As shown below, based on its review of Inspector General reports, GAO identified fraud risks affecting Medicare that CPI did not identify or assess as part of its VM Process.
Fraud Risks That CPI Did Not Identity or Assess in Its Risk Assessment
Further, CPI’s VM Process does not align with other leading practices that would help it strategically manage Medicare fraud risks. Specifically, the VM Process does not include an assessment of the likelihood and impact of fraud risks or examine the suitability of existing mitigating fraud controls for Medicare. For example, CPI identified a vulnerability associated with the supplier enrollment screening process, which GAO identified as a significant fraud risk, given its association with cases of alleged Medicare fraud. However, CPI’s risk assessment did not assess the likelihood and impact of this vulnerability as a fraud risk. Without including such an assessment, CPI risks overlooking the full scope and impact of fraud risks.
Why GAO Did This Study
Medicare is the largest federal health program. The Medicare program was first included in GAO’s High Risk List in 1990 and remains on the list due to its size, complexity, effect on the federal budget and health care sector, and continued susceptibility to fraud, mismanagement, and improper payments. GAO was asked to review HHS’s efforts to prevent and minimize fraud in Medicare. This report evaluates, among other things, the extent to which HHS has assessed fraud risks in Medicare.
GAO reviewed documentation related to risk assessments for Medicare and related guidance. GAO also analyzed HHS Inspector General reports, federal court documents, and interviews from various contractors to identify Medicare fraud risks. GAO interviewed and reviewed information reported from HHS’s Office of the Assistant Secretary for Financial Resources, CMS, and CPI. GAO compared this information against relevant leading practices from GAO’s Fraud Risk Framework and internal control requirements.
